wind noun

also blast, gust, the wind is picking up, the wind is dying down, the wind changed

classical

Traupman 137, 407

ventus, ventī m.

noun, second declension

Other words

  • flātus, flātūs m. — a blast, a gust

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Hor. AP 205; Ov. M. 13.418 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 135

    (mostly poetic (Lewis & Short))

Examples

  • ventus flat

    the wind is blowingcomposed

  • Ventus increbrēscit.

    The wind is picking up.Traupman 137; cf. Cic. Fam. 7.20.3: ventus (Lewis & Short s.v. increbrēscō)

  • Ventus dētumēscit.

    The wind is dying down.Traupman 137

  • Ventus sē vertit.

    The wind changed.Traupman 289

See also west wind.

SourcesThe example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
